items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What did you learn from people like Betty Carter and Dexter Gordon, that generation. ... [INTERVIEWEE] A lot of everything. A lot of music, but partly more life than anything. Because one thing about Betty that I always admired was her strength...

ctx.x: Louis Hayes, Sam Jones. But I mean Roy McCurdy is a good friend. I love that band too. But all the bands were good, but it was just the way that Cannonball played, the way he approached the music. Everything, I mean the dance was in the music. That’s the key. When you heard Cannonball I mean it would get you dancing. The dance was in the music and everything they played sounded fun. It reached you. It hit you in the soul. And it was funny because one of the bands I had later on I remember I had George Cables play…

He did. He played like he was, I mean he just played with his personality almost. He just was so erudite and, that was great. Great stuff. What did you learn from people like Betty Carter and Dexter Gordon, that generation. Anything that you can pass on?

A lot of everything. A lot of music, but partly more life than anything. Because one thing about Betty that I always admired was her strength, and she was tenacious. She was going to find a way to get it done. And we miss that. And I think the music misses that, those kind of people like that. Betty, you know, she would think — if a door was closed she used to go open up something somewhere else. Because I remember many times just asking her questions all the time. And she had ways of, okay well if this club is…
